'''Renata Elizaveta Kallosh''' ({{langx|ru|Рената Елизавета (Эрнестовна) Каллош}}; {{langx|uk|Рената Єлизавета Каллош}}; born 1943) is a Russian-American [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]]. She is a professor of physics at [[Stanford University]], working there on [[supergravity]], [[string theory]] and [[inflationary cosmology]].

==Biography==
Kallosh was born in 1943 in [[Chernivtsi]].{{cn|date=January 2025}} She completed her Bachelor's from [[Moscow State University]] in 1966 and obtained her Ph.D. from [[Lebedev Physical Institute]], Moscow in 1968. She was then a professor at the same Institute, before moving to [[CERN]] for a year in 1989. Kallosh joined Stanford in 1990. In 2022 she retired, but continues her research as a member of Stanford Institute for Theoretical Physics.

In 2009 she received the Lise Meitner Award of the Gothenburg University.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gothenburg Lise Meitner Award|url=https://www.chalmers.se/en/centres/gpc/activities/lisemeitner/Pages/default.aspx|access-date=27 December 2019}}</ref> In 2014 awarded Doctorate Honoris Causa of the University of Groningen. In 2017 she was awarded Lorentz Chair position at the University of Leiden,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lorentz.leidenuniv.nl/lorentzchair/|title=Lorentz Chair |access-date=27 December 2019}}</ref> and became a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/renata-kallosh|title=Renata Kallosh|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=27 December 2019}}</ref> In 2024 she gave the  Oskar Klein Memorial Lecture at Stockholm University and was awarded the Oscar Klein medal for her work on black hole attractors, supergravity and cosmology.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_yjqwqrDKu4/|title=Oskar Klein Memorial Lecture|access-date=9 December 2024}}</ref> 

Kallosh is best known for her contributions to the theory of [[supergravity]] — the supersymmetric generalization of [[Albert Einstein|Einstein]]'s theory of [[gravity]]. She was the first to quantize supergravity, obtaining the full set of Feynman rules including a new, unexpected ghost particle (now called the Nielsen-Kallosh ghost).<ref>{{cite journal|title=Modified Feynman rules in supergravity|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=141|issue=1–2|pages=141–152|year=1978|author=Kallosh, Renata|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(78)90340-1|bibcode=1978NuPhB.141..141K|issn=0550-3213|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1060533}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Ghost counting in supergravity|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=140|issue=3|page=449|year=1978|author=Nielsen, Niels|bibcode=1978NuPhB.140..449K|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(78)90009-3}}</ref> This paper also gave one of the first applications of [[BRST quantization|BRST symmetry]]<ref>{{cite journal|title=Renormalization of gauge theories|journal=Annals of Physics|volume=98|issue=2|page=287|year=1976|author1=Becchi, C.|author2=Rouet, A.|author3=Stora, Raymond|bibcode=1976AnPhy..98..287B|doi=10.1016/0003-4916(76)90156-1|url=http://www.numdam.org/item/RCP25_1975__22__A10_0/}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Gauge invariance in field theory and statistical physics in operator formalism|journal=Lebedev Institute Report|volume=39|year=1975|author=Tyutin, Igor V.}}</ref> to express the gauge invariances of gravity, and, incidentally, introduced the name "BRST". She also was the first to understand the structure of divergences in quantum theories of supergravity, showing, among other results, that supergravity with N=8 supersymmetry is finite at least up to 8 loops.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Counterterms in extended supergravity|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=99|issue=2|page=122|year=1981|author=Kallosh, Renata|bibcode=1981PhLB...99..122K|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(81)90964-3|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/125864}}</ref> She is the author of many papers on [[black hole]] solutions in supergravity theories. A particularly influential work is the recognition, in collaboration with Sergio Ferrara, that black hole solutions with higher supersymmetry have properties similar to attractor solutions of mechanical systems.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Supersymmetry and attractors|journal=Physical Review D|volume=54|issue=2|pages=1514–1524|year=1996|arxiv=hep-th/9602136|author=Ferrara, Sergio|author2=Kallosh, Renata|bibcode=1996PhRvD..54.1514F|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.54.1514|pmid=10020825|s2cid=5137358}}</ref>

Kallosh is also known<ref>{{cite web|title=INSPIRE Citations Summary for Author "kallosh,renata"|url=http://inspirehep.net/search?ln=en&p=a+kallosh%2Crenata&of=hb&action_search=Search&sf=earliestdate&so=d|access-date=13 May 2018}}</ref> for her contributions to [[string theory]]. In particular, she, along with [[Sandip Trivedi]], [[Andrei Linde]], and [[Shamit Kachru]], found the mechanism to stabilize string theory vacua<ref>{{cite journal|title=de Sitter Vacua in String Theory|journal=Physical Review D|volume=68|issue=4|article-number=046005|arxiv=hep-th/0301240|author=Kachru, Shamit|author2=Kallosh, Renata|author3=Linde, Andrei|author4=Trivedi, Sandip P.|year=2003|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.68.046005|bibcode=2003PhRvD..68d6005K|s2cid=119482182}}</ref> referred to as [[KKLT mechanism]] after the authors' last names. This mechanism provided a possible theoretical explanation of the anomalously small value of [[vacuum energy]] ([[cosmological constant]]) and a description of the present stage of the accelerated expansion of the universe in the context of the theory of inflationary [[multiverse]]<ref>{{cite journal|title=de Sitter Vacua in String Theory|journal=Reports on Progress in Physics|volume=80|issue=2|page=022001|arxiv=1512.01203|author=Linde, Andrei|year=2015|bibcode=2015arXiv151201203L|doi=10.1088/1361-6633/aa50e4|pmid=28071600|s2cid=5221573}}</ref> and [[string theory landscape]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=The Cosmic Landscape: String Theory and the Illusion of Intelligent Design (Publisher: Little, Brown and Company)|url=https://archive.org/details/cosmiclandscapes00suss|url-access=registration|author=Susskind, Leonard|year=2005|publisher=Little, Brown and Company |isbn=978-0-316-15579-3 }}</ref>

After the discovery of the KKLT mechanism, her interests shifted towards investigation of cosmological implications of supergravity and string theory. In particular, Renata Kallosh and [[Andrei Linde]], together with their collaborators, developed a theory of cosmological attractors. This is a broad class of versions of [[inflationary cosmology]] which provide one of the best fits to the latest observational data.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Planck 2015 results. XX. Constraints on inflation|journal=Astronomy and Astrophysics|volume=594|issue=A20|pages=A20|arxiv=1502.02114|author=Ade, P.A.R.|display-authors=etal|year=2016|doi=10.1051/0004-6361/201525898|doi-access=free|bibcode=2016A&A...594A..20P|s2cid=119284788}}</ref>
